learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected Still 67% and locked the prediction for the top word after lowering temperature from 1 to 0.5 with scores 2, 1 and 0.
observations.exploration: At 0.5, twenty draws were 17 mat, 2 sofa and 1 moon. At 4, they were 8, 6 and 6, with displayed probabilities 41.9%, 32.6% and 25.4%. At 1, twenty draws were 16, 2 and 2. Candidate words stayed unchanged.
observations.reveal: The reveal corrected the answer to about 87%, gave exact 86.7%, and explained dividing scores by temperature changes gaps. It accurately quoted the cool and hot samples, distinguished spreading choices from learning new information, and gave the exponential probability rule.
observations.visual: Inspected the inline dark 1257 by 936 screenshot at temperature 4. Three colored horizontal bars showed the more even probabilities, with score divisions and sampled dot counts beneath each word.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884163 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: The prompt targets a specific misconception about probability scaling.
prediction.evidence: Selected unchanged odds before trying the cooler setting.

interaction.reason: Temperature changes expose the same candidates with different probability gaps and samples.
interaction.evidence: Cool draws concentrated on mat, while hot draws spread across all three words.

payoff.reason: The reveal ties actual draws to score gap scaling and a clear limitation.
payoff.evidence: It quoted both samples and explained that the menu did not change.

clarity.reason: Bars, score divisions and sample dots separate probabilities from realized draws.
clarity.evidence: Hot probabilities and 8/6/6 draws were shown together.

transfer.reason: The ending applies the rule to interpreting a real model sampling setting.
transfer.evidence: Higher temperature spreads existing choices rather than teaching the model new information.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: Hotter output can be explained without adding any knowledge or candidates.
surprise.evidence: Only the probabilities changed across the fixed mat, sofa and moon menu.

visualExplanation.reason: Bar flattening and transformed score gaps show the mechanism.
visualExplanation.evidence: At temperature 4 the scores became 0.5, 0.25 and 0.

playfulness.reason: Sampling familiar sentence completions makes probability changes tangible.
playfulness.evidence: Each press produced a visible twenty word sample.

practicalValue.reason: It clarifies what a generation temperature control does.
practicalValue.evidence: The reveal connects the same rule to language model sampling.

depth.reason: It distinguishes candidate set, score scaling, probability and sample variability.
depth.evidence: The exact rule and actual samples appear in the reveal.

complexity.reason: The bars and familiar words are accessible, while exponential normalization and randomness add novelty.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Moderate: separate score, probability and observed frequency.
complexity.conceptualChallenge: Dividing scores changes relative probability gaps without changing knowledge.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Sampling temperature and exponential probability are introduced.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Moderate to high in the final formula; the visual comparison works without calculating it.

whyCool: A creative sounding setting can be watched simply redistributing the same three choices.
caveat: Only one fixed three word score vector is tested; sample counts are not the theoretical probabilities.
missingEvidence: No fresh score vector or extended generated text was tested.
